tip_title: Your Home Policy Has Two Ways to Pay for Damaged Belongings. Most People Don't Know Which One They Have.
topic: Home Insurance - Personal Property Settlement Method (ACV vs. Replacement Cost)
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Your Home Policy Has Two Ways to Pay for Damaged Belongings. Most People Don't Know Which One They Have.**

When something inside your home gets damaged or destroyed — furniture, electronics, clothing, whatever — your policy pays out in one of two ways. Actual cash value (ACV) pays you what the item is worth today, after depreciation. Replacement cost coverage pays you what it actually costs to buy that item new. The difference on a five-year-old laptop or a sofa isn't trivial. A couch that cost $1,200 might have an ACV of $400 and a replacement cost of $1,400. If you've got ACV coverage on your personal property, that gap comes out of your pocket. With the holidays coming and people bringing home new gifts and gear, this is worth a quick check on your declarations page — look for "personal property settlement method" and see which one applies to your policy.

Not sure what your policy says? Your Peachy agent can pull that up and walk you through it in a few minutes.

📖 [Learn more from NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/insurance/homeowners/learn/actual-cash-value-vs-replacement-cost)
